rows.en: @My big sister taught it to me.
rows.jp: 「お姉ちゃんに / 教えてもらったんだ
rows.lit: My big sister taught it to me.
rows.re: My big sister taught it to me.
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @I want to be like my sister. I want to create my own charm to make people smile.
rows.jp: 「わたしも、お姉ちゃんみたいになるんだ / 誰かを<b:8a5b>探にさせる / おまじないを見つけるんだ〜
rows.lit: I'll become like my big sister: I'll find a charm that makes people smile.
rows.re: I'll become like my big sister. / I'll find a charm that makes / people smile.
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @Well, then, let's get busy!
rows.jp: 「じゃあ / そうと決まれば急がなくっちゃッ！
rows.lit: Well then, now that it's decided, we'd better hurry!
rows.re: Well then, now that it's decided, / we'd better hurry!
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @Hmm. Let me see that for a minute.
rows.jp: 「ちょっと<b:8b19><b:8a9a>するの<b:8b6c>発の<b:8b72>撃をね、異空間に<b:8a85>着する / <b:8b33>利な魔法<b:8b6c><b:8b29>があったんだよ〜
rows.lit: Let me borrow a look at that a moment.
rows.re: Let me borrow a look at that a / moment.
rows.speaker: McGregor

rows.en: @Hey... That's strange.
rows.jp: 「あっれ〜 / おかしいな〜<b:8b6c>破するつもりだったのか？
rows.lit: Huh? That's odd...
rows.re: Huh? That's odd...
rows.speaker: Lilka
SKIPPED - no content box in decode

rows.en: >Only you-know-who could have pulled off something like this.
rows.jp: ＞こんなことができるのは / ヤツらしかいない
rows.lit: Only that lot could have pulled this off.
rows.re: Only that lot could have pulled / this off.
rows.speaker: commander

rows.en: >I need your help.
rows.jp: ＞貴様らの出番だ
rows.lit: It's your turn to act.
rows.re: It's your turn to act.
rows.speaker: commander

rows.en: >The data tablets' ID pattern was detected moving 1southwest0 out of Sielje.
rows.jp: ＞データタブレットから<b:8b73>知される / <8947>作パターンは / シエルジェより[11]お先東の方<894b>[11]ぉに移動中
rows.lit: The pattern sensed from the data tablets is moving from Sielje toward the region yonder-east.
rows.re: The pattern sensed from the data / tablets is moving from Sielje / toward the |east yonder|.
rows.speaker: commander

rows.en: >I want you to begin pursuit immediately.
rows.jp: ＞ただちに / 追跡にあたってほしい
rows.lit: I want you to begin pursuit at once.
rows.re: I want you to begin pursuit at / once.
rows.speaker: commander

rows.en: @Ah ha! They're going to go through Gate Bridge!
rows.jp: 「そうかッ！ / ゲートブリッジを抜けるつもりだな
rows.lit: I see! They mean to slip through the Gate Bridge!
rows.re: I see! They mean to slip through / the Gate Bridge!
rows.speaker: party

rows.en: @This key will get you across Gate Bridge. Take it with you.
rows.jp: 「こいつがゲートを渡るのに必要なカギだ / 持っていくがいいよ放を試みている事が〜
rows.lit: This is the key you need to cross the Gate; take it with you.
rows.re: This is the key you need to cross / the Gate. Take it with you.
rows.speaker: NPC

rows.en: (Wait a sec... How did they even find out we were in Sielje?)
rows.jp: （それよりも〜 / シエルジェ自分領に<b:8b74>れている事が / 連中にわかったのだろう〜？
rows.lit: (More to the point: how did they know we were staying in the Sielje domain?)
rows.re: (More to the point: how did they / know we were staying in the / Sielje domain?)
rows.speaker: Brad, thinking

rows.en: (Could someone be feeding them information? No! It couldn't be!)
rows.jp: （まさか、街通者が〜 / いや、そんなことは<b:8af2>対に〜）
rows.lit: (Could there be an informer? No; that could never be...)
rows.re: (Could there be an informer? No. / That could never be...)
rows.speaker: Brad, thinking

rows.en: @A Spell Bomb that sends a bomb blast between dimensions. Don't you remember that from class?
rows.jp: 「異世界に<b:8b6c>発の<b:8b72>撃を / <b:8a85>移させる結単な魔法<b:8b6c><b:8b29><f040><f042> / 授業で<b:8a8a>っただろ？
rows.lit: A simple Spell Bomb that shunts the blast into another dimension; we learned it in class, right?
rows.re: A simple Spell Bomb that shunts / the blast into another dimension. / We learned it in class!
rows.speaker: rival

rows.jp: [17]<b:8b75>違いするなよなッ！
rows.speaker: SKIPPED - no content box in decode

rows.en: @You'd better not get killed out there, 'cause when you get back, we're going head to head!
rows.jp: 「無事に帰って来いよ / 帰ってきたら / 俺と勝負するんだッ！
rows.lit: Come back safe; and when you do, you're facing me in a showdown!
rows.re: Come back safe. And when you do, / you're facing me in a showdown!
rows.speaker: rival

rows.en: @And let me tell you...
rows.jp: 「そして今度こそは<f040><f042>負けないから
rows.lit: And this time, for sure...
rows.re: And this time, for sure...
rows.speaker: rival

rows.en: @I don't have time for this now!
rows.jp: 「こんなところで / 立ち止まってられないの
rows.lit: I can't be standing still in a place like this!
rows.re: I can't be standing still in a / place like this!
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @Catch ya later!
rows.jp: 「じゃあねッ！
rows.lit: See you!
rows.re: See you!
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @No matter how many times I measure it, I get the same results.
rows.jp: 「<f040><f042>そして、何度やっても / 特待結果は同じです〜
rows.lit: And no matter how many times we measure, the result is the same.
rows.re: And no matter how many times we / measure, the result is the same.
rows.speaker: observer

rows.en: @It's a huge thermonuclear mass near Sector 326 in Cradle Constellation and it's heading for Filgaia!
rows.jp: 「ゆりかご<8860>方<b:8a76>、３２６付近に / <88bf>大な<8868>核反応を確認ッ！ / 現在、ファルガイアに向かって搭近中
rows.lit: A massive thermonuclear reaction confirmed near Sector 326, Cradle quadrant! Now closing on Filgaia!
rows.re: A massive thermonuclear reaction / near Sector 326, Cradle quadrant! / Now closing on Filgaia!
rows.speaker: observer

rows.en: @We matched it against the patterns Guild Galad gave us, and it looks like the nuclear weapon Grauswein.
rows.jp: 「ギルドグラードから<b:8ac3>族された / パターン<b:8acd>合の結果 / 核同時『グラウスヴァイン』と思われます
rows.speaker: SKIPPED - no content box in decode

rows.en: *Do you want to read it?2
rows.jp: ＊進みますか？[18]か
rows.lit: Do you want to proceed?
rows.re: Do you want to proceed?
rows.speaker: examine prompt

rows.en: @Unfortunately, this service is unavailable in the Demo Version.
rows.jp: 「<f040><f042>でも、今回の体験版では / 残念ながら使用することができません
rows.lit: But in this trial version, it unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.re: But in this trial version, it / unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.speaker: system: demo notice

rows.en: *Unfortunately, this service is unavailable in the Demo Version.
rows.jp: ＊〜ですが、今回の体験版では / 残念ながら使用することができません
rows.lit: ...however, in this trial version it unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.re: ...however, in this trial version, / it unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.speaker: system: demo notice

rows.en: @Why is it that people never try to do anything to help the world until a serious danger comes along?
rows.jp: 「でも、いけませんね〜 / 本当に危険な目にあわないと / 立ち上がろうとしないなんて〜
rows.lit: But it's no good, is it: refusing to stand up until real danger strikes.
rows.re: But it's no good, is it: refusing / to stand up until real danger / strikes.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But people aren't that worried anymore, because so far nothing bad has happened to them.
rows.jp: 「<8a1b>体的に<889a><889b>を右けないから / 誰も、危機信を乗れさせているけど / これこそ危険なことなのでは？
rows.lit: Since no concrete harm has come, everyone's let their sense of danger slip; isn't that itself the danger?
rows.re: Since no concrete harm has come, / everyone's let their guard slip. / Isn't that the danger?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Until the other day, I had forgotten how serious things are.
rows.jp: 「私もこのあいだまで / 危機信を失っていましたが〜
rows.lit: I too had lost my sense of danger until the other day.
rows.re: I too had lost my sense of danger / until the other day.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But nothing really terrible happened down here, so after a while, the shock wore off.
rows.jp: 「でも、とくに大きな発ぎが / 起きたわけじゃないから / <b:8a38>々に<b:8a39>れてきちゃったわ
rows.lit: But since no great uproar came of it, little by little the shock wore off.
rows.re: But since no great uproar came of / it, little by little the shock / wore off.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I use the past tense because Archheim is a city of the past. A lost city.
rows.jp: 「そう、過去面で<b:8a3b>られるように / アークハイムは / 失われた、過去の場なのです<b:8a3c>の娘エリザは / <b:8a3e><8a0e>を<b:8a3f>ったスレイハイム解放軍を / ひどく恨んでいました
rows.lit: Yes: as it is told in the past tense, Archheim is a lost city of the past.
rows.re: Yes: as it is told in the past / tense, Archheim is a lost city of / the past.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But she was just a young girl unable to act on her anger. At some point, she disappeared.
rows.jp: 「ですが、数幼き娘に / 何ができるものではなく / やがて、この地より<b:8a43>を消したのです
rows.lit: But there was nothing a young girl could do, and in time she vanished from this land.
rows.re: But there was nothing a young / girl could do, and in time she / vanished from this land.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @If she still lives, she must be a beautiful, full-grown woman by now. I wonder what she's doing now.
rows.jp: 「生きていれば / <b:8a44>しく成長しているはず / 今は、どこで何をしているのか〜一家、ヴィクトリア<b:8a3c>は / 穏健派であるにもかかわらず / 解放軍によって処断されたのです
rows.lit: If she lives, she must have grown beautiful; where is she now, and what is she doing?
rows.re: If she lives, she must have grown / beautiful. Where is she now, and / what is she doing?
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Only the daughter, Eliza, survived. She harbored a fierce hatred for the Liberation Army.
rows.jp: 「残されたひとり娘のエリザ<b:8a4a>は / 解放軍に強い恨みを / いだいていたといいますが〜
rows.lit: The sole surviving daughter, Eliza, is said to have harbored a fierce grudge against the Liberation Army.
rows.re: The sole surviving daughter, / Eliza, harbored a fierce grudge / against the Liberation Army.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @After the civil war, the Liberation Army disbanded, and Eliza lost her chance to get revenge.
rows.jp: 「街戦の<8865>後、解放軍も<b:8a4b>解してしまい / エリザ<b:8a4a>の恨みははらせぬまま / 今にいたっているのです
rows.lit: Right after the civil war the Army disbanded, and Eliza's grudge remains unavenged to this day.
rows.re: Right after the war the Army / disbanded, and Eliza's grudge / remains unavenged to this day.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Just like you fought back, right?
rows.jp: 「そう〜 / あなたたちのようにね
rows.lit: Yes... just like you all did.
rows.re: Yes... just like you all did.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Who knows what they'll do. It's frightening just to think of it.
rows.jp: 「だからこそ / ここからの動きが / 恐ろしいのよ〜
rows.lit: That is exactly why their next move is so frightening.
rows.re: That is exactly why their next / move is so frightening.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @A big group came here to buy food and weapons. They were part of your team, right?
rows.jp: 「大勢でやってきて / 武器とか食料とかを調達していたのは / あなたと、その仲間だったわよね
rows.lit: The big group that came buying weapons and food; that was you and your companions, wasn't it?
rows.re: The big group that came buying / weapons and food; that was you / and your companions, wasn't it?
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @They bought whatever they could get their hands on, then headed for the southern desert. Was that Odessa?
rows.jp: 「大<886f>の物資をかき集めて / 先の<88db>の道に向かっていったそうじゃない / あれがウワサのオデッサかしら？限
rows.lit: They gathered up masses of supplies and headed for the desert yonder, I hear; was that the famous Odessa?
rows.re: They gathered masses of supplies / and headed for the desert yonder. / Was that the famous Odessa?
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @Just like this strange phenomenon.
rows.jp: 「この<b:8a51>変地異も、そう〜
rows.lit: This cataclysm too, the same.
rows.re: This cataclysm too, the same.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @This threat affects everyone in Filgaia. It's taken all the fun out of gossiping.
rows.jp: 「ファルガイアに生きる全員に / ふりかかる脅威だから / ウワサを聞いてもおもしろくなんかないわ
rows.lit: It's a threat falling on everyone in Filgaia, so even gossip about it brings no fun.
rows.re: It's a threat falling on everyone / in Filgaia, so even gossip brings / no fun.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @I'm a little nervous, but to be honest, I'm not afraid.
rows.jp: 「たしかに不安はあるけど / 正<8865>言って、恐れはないの
rows.lit: There's unease, certainly; but honestly speaking, no fear.
rows.re: There's unease, certainly. But / honestly speaking, no fear.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @It's as if my senses have been numbed by the strangeness of what's happening.
rows.jp: 「あまりにも / 非世<b:8a54>な出<b:8a55>事ばかりだから / どこか信信がマヒしているのかも〜民衆の味方だった一家まで / まとめて処断されたってハナシじゃない
rows.lit: With nothing but unearthly events, perhaps my senses have gone numb somewhere.
rows.re: With nothing but unearthly / events, perhaps my senses have / gone numb somewhere.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @The Slayheim Liberation Army may seem like heroes, but they have a lot of dark secrets.
rows.jp: 「スレイハイム解放戦役っていうと / 何だかカッコイイけれど / いろいろと暗いウワサは<b:8a59>えないわ
rows.lit: "The Slayheim Liberation War" sounds gallant, but the dark rumors around it never fade.
rows.re: The Slayheim Liberation War / sounds gallant, but the dark / rumors around it never fade.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @War is war, no matter how lofty some people may try to make it seem.
rows.jp: 「そうよね / どんなに取り<b:8a5a>っても / 戦争は戦争だもの<b:8a5c>合して / 塩の原野で覆ってしまっても / ５数前の悲<b:8a61>は消えないものよ
rows.lit: That's right: dress it up however you like, war is war.
rows.re: That's right: dress it up however / you like, war is war.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @That's because people will always gossip about what happened.
rows.jp: 「人が生きている限り / ウワサは口の端にのぼるもんだからね<b:8a64><b:8a65>のために役立てたい / ３．ウワサならアテにならない[1a]が塩にのまれた原野に / かつてのスレイハイムの都 / アークハイムが今なおあるみたいだね
rows.lit: As long as people live, rumor will find its way to their lips.
rows.re: As long as people live, rumor / will find its way to their lips.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @They say it's a town of the dead, inhabited by tormented souls that can't rest.
rows.jp: 「今となっては / 浮かばれない<b:8a68>がさまよう / 死者の場となっているとか〜塩の鍵が見えてくるわ
rows.lit: Now, they say, it's a city of the dead where unquiet souls wander.
rows.re: Now, they say, it's a city of the / dead where unquiet souls wander.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @That's where Archheim, capital of Slayheim, used to be.
rows.jp: 「そこは、スレイハイムの王都 / アークハイムがあった場所なのよ
rows.lit: That's where Archheim, Slayheim's royal capital, once stood.
rows.re: That's where Archheim, Slayheim's / royal capital, once stood.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @Archheim once prospered because of the Live Reflector there.
rows.jp: 「アークハイムには / ライブリフレクターが備えられていて / それを中心に栄えていたの
rows.lit: Archheim had a Live Reflector, and flourished around it.
rows.re: Archheim had a Live Reflector, / and flourished around it.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @But in the civil war 5 years ago, the city's splendor and life was engulfed in a sea of salt.
rows.jp: 「でも、５数前の街戦で / かつての栄<b:8a6a>も人の命も / 全部、塩にのまれてしまったけどね
rows.lit: But in the civil war five years back, its old glory and its people's lives were all swallowed by the salt.
rows.re: But in the civil war five years / back, its glory and its people / were swallowed by the salt.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @The area is haunted by the ghosts of the people of Archheim, they say.
rows.jp: 「今や、アークハイムの<b:8a6b>人は / 浮かばれない亡者ばかりと聞いてるわ
rows.lit: Now, I hear, Archheim's only residents are the restless dead.
rows.re: Now, I hear, Archheim's only / residents are the restless dead.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @You'd better take this so that you don't end up as one of them.
rows.jp: 「これでも持っていって / 彼らの仲間にならないように / 気をつけなさいよ真実は<b:8a6d>まれているものよ
rows.lit: Take this with you, and mind you don't end up joining their number.
rows.re: Take this with you, and mind you / don't end up joining their / number.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @What's important is the wisdom to see the truth in any rumor.
rows.jp: 「ようするに、見<b:8a6e>めるための / 判断力が大事ってことね民衆の味方だった一家まで / まとめて処断されたってハナシじゃない
rows.lit: In short, what matters is the judgment to see through to the truth.
rows.re: In short, what matters is the / judgment to see through to the / truth.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @The Slayheim Liberation Army may seem like heroes, but they have a lot of dark secrets.
rows.jp: 「スレイハイム解放戦役っていうと / 何だかカッコイイけれど / いろいろと暗いウワサは<b:8a59>えないわ
rows.lit: "The Slayheim Liberation War" sounds grand, but the dark rumors around it never quite fade.
rows.re: |The Slayheim Liberation War| / sounds grand, but the dark / rumors never quite fade.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @War is war, no matter how lofty some people may try to make it seem.
rows.jp: 「そうよね / どんなに取り<b:8a5a>っても / 戦争は戦争だもの<b:8a6f>きというだけで / まゆをひそめる人もいるけれど / これは私なりの情報斬集なのよ知るものではないものね
rows.lit: That's right; dress it up however you like, war is war.
rows.re: That's right; dress it up however / you like, war is war.
rows.speaker: townswoman

rows.en: @but there's something that's been bothering me.
rows.jp: 「ちょっと / 気になることがあるのよね
rows.lit: There's just one thing that's been bothering me.
rows.re: There's just one thing that's / been bothering me.
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @Have you noticed that wherever you go, your foes, Odessa, always appear there, too?
rows.jp: 「どうしてあんたたちの行くところ / 相であるオデッサが / 必ず現われるのかしら？
rows.lit: Why is it that wherever you go, your foe Odessa is sure to appear?
rows.re: Why is it that wherever you go, / your foe Odessa is sure to / appear?
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @Could it be that information about what you're doing is being leaked to Odessa?
rows.jp: 「もしかして / あんたたちの情報が / 向こうに<b:8a71>抜けなんじゃないの？
rows.lit: Could it be your information is leaking straight through to them?
rows.re: Could it be your information is / leaking straight through to them?
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @So how is it that wherever you go, Odessa always seems to be waiting there for you?
rows.jp: 「なのに、行く先々で / オデッサに出くわすなんて / 不思議な話だとは思わない？
rows.lit: And yet you run into Odessa at every turn; doesn't that strike you as strange?
rows.re: And yet you run into Odessa at / every turn. Doesn't that strike / you as strange?
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @There must be a spy in your midst!
rows.jp: 「そうよッ！ / スパイよ、密告者、街通者よッ！
rows.lit: That's it! A spy! An informer! A collaborator!
rows.re: That's it! A spy! An informer! A / collaborator!
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @There just HAS to be! I'm sure of it!
rows.jp: 「きっとそういうのが / いるに違わないわッ！
rows.lit: There must be one among you, I'm sure of it!
rows.re: There must be one among you, I'm / sure of it!
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @You must have some idea of who it could be...
rows.jp: 「気をつけてごらんなさい / ホラ、心当たりが / あるんじゃないかしら〜<b:8a64>時にあっては<88f6><889b>なのかもしれません
rows.lit: Look sharp; see, doesn't someone come to mind?
rows.re: Look sharp. See, doesn't someone / come to mind?
rows.speaker: gossip

rows.en: @Or it could be a large-scale disaster, something with massive powers. Or...
rows.jp: 「それも大きな<88f6><889b>〜 / <b:8a73><889b>、<b:8a73><b:8a74>と呼ばれるような / <88bf>大な力が、あるいは〜<b:8a75>げとなっていた / 大地の<b:8a76><b:8a77>、ビッグバレー〜
rows.lit: Or some great calamity; a vast power of the kind called disaster; or else...
rows.re: Or some great calamity, a vast / power of the kind called / disaster. Or else...
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But it did stop the land from being completely engulfed in salt.
rows.jp: 「ですが、大地が完全に塩にのまれるのを / 阻止してくれたのも事実なのです
rows.lit: And yet it is also fact that it kept the land from being wholly swallowed by the salt.
rows.re: And yet it is also fact that it / kept the land from being wholly / swallowed by the salt.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @You never know how something is going to benefit you.
rows.jp: 「世の中、いったい何が / うまく作用するのかわからないものです<b:8a78>てるのでしょう？
rows.lit: In this world, one never knows what will turn out to work for the good.
rows.re: In this world, one never knows / what will turn out to work for / the good.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @This planet has already been ruined. There's nothing to be so surprised about now.
rows.jp: 「ここはかつて / 大地を失った世界〜 / 今さら<8845>きはしませんよ野[11]ぉにて / 塩にのみこまれた場を発見しても / そこには近づかない方がいいですよ
rows.lit: This was a world that lost its land once already; nothing surprises me now.
rows.re: This was a world that lost its / land once already. Nothing / surprises me now.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @It is what's left of Archheim, heart of the former Slayheim Kingdom.
rows.jp: 「その<b:8a79>都の名はアークハイム〜 / スレイハイム国の中心ともいえる / 大きな場の亡<b:8a7b>です<b:8a7c>次の遺<b:8a7d>が / 年多く<89bb>っているそうです
rows.lit: The ruined capital's name is Archheim: the ghost of a great city, heart of the Slayheim nation.
rows.re: The ruined capital's name is / Archheim: the ghost of a great / city, heart of Slayheim.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @The Mercs are convinced they'll strike it rich there, but I have my doubts.
rows.jp: 「渡り左たちが / 一<b:8a7e><b:8a7f>金を<b:8a80>見ているそうですが / さて、うまくいくのでしょうか？塩に覆われた原野が広がっています
rows.lit: The Drifters, I hear, dream of striking it rich there; will it go well, I wonder?
rows.re: The Drifters, I hear, dream of / striking it rich there. Will it / go well, I wonder?
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Buried in the sand are the remains of the former military superpower of Slayheim.
rows.jp: 「その塩の辺には / かつて、スレイハイムと呼ばれた / 軍事大国があったのです〜<b:8a76><b:8a77>、ビッグバレーにかけられた / 谷の<89ec>の上にできた場なんですよ<b:8a81><b:8a82>を呼び / 悲しみを<b:8a83>く〜
rows.lit: In that salt waste there once stood the military great power called Slayheim.
rows.re: In that salt waste there once / stood the military great power / called Slayheim.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But the weak-hearted may also be more willing to turn to others and join hands with them for help.
rows.jp: 「だけど、弱い心ゆえに / 手を取り合い協力していくすべを / 知っているものなのかもしれない<b:8a85>に対して / <b:8a86>国一<88a8>で<88cc>撃にあたったらしいな
rows.lit: And yet perhaps it is the weak-hearted who know the way of joining hands and working together.
rows.re: And yet perhaps it is the weak- / hearted who know the way of / joining hands together.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @This would have been unthinkable in the past. But today, nations are joining in unity.
rows.jp: 「以前では考えられなかったことだ / 国と国、人と人とが / 手を取り合っていくなんて…<b:8a81>う心ってのは / どんなに小さな一帯でも / <b:8a38>々に広がって、心を<b:8a87>んでいく
rows.lit: It would have been unthinkable before: nation with nation, person with person, joining hands...
rows.re: It would have been unthinkable / before: nation with nation, / person with person, joined...
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @In the end, the heart is devoured, just as the sky was.
rows.jp: 「最後には / この空のようになっちまうものさ<b:8a81>われるようなことが / あったんじゃないのか？
rows.lit: In the end, it all winds up like this sky.
rows.re: In the end, it all winds up like / this sky.
rows.speaker: cynic

rows.en: @If you truly believed in your friend, you could have found a way to disprove your suspicions.
rows.jp: 「あんたも本当に仲間を信じているなら / <b:8a81>いを<b:8a88>らす方法だって / あったと僕は思うぜ仲間を<b:8a81>わせてしまったかもな / 〜悪かったと思ってる<b:8a81>うってのは / それだけ心が弱いからさ
rows.lit: If you truly trusted your companion, I reckon there was a way to clear the doubt.
rows.re: If you truly trusted your / companion, I reckon there was a / way to clear the doubt.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But then, someone with no weaknesses at all would be flawed as a human being.
rows.jp: 「でもよ、弱さを<89b8><b:8a89>も持っていない / 完<b:8a8a>な心を持っているヤツは / 人間として、どこか欠けているに違いない
rows.lit: But a fellow with a perfect heart and not a scrap of weakness must be lacking somewhere as a human.
rows.re: But a fellow with a perfect heart / and not a scrap of weakness must / be lacking as a human.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Don't you think so?
rows.jp: 「そう、思わないか？
rows.lit: Don't you think so?
rows.re: Don't you think so?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @You were with that shady-looking bunch that came to town!
rows.jp: 「あんた、あやしい連中とつるんで / 近頃この場に出<b:8a8b>しているよな？
rows.lit: You've been hanging with that shady lot, coming and going here lately, haven't you?
rows.re: You've been hanging with that / shady lot, coming and going here / lately, haven't you?
rows.speaker: suspicious NPC

rows.en: @You aren't part of that terrorist group, Odessa, are you?
rows.jp: 「あんた、まさか / テロリスト・オデッサに / <b:8a8c>しているんじゃないだろうな仲間の誰とは言わないけど / 武装した一団といっしょに行動しているのを / 僕は確かに見たんだ
rows.lit: Don't tell me you're mixed up with the terrorists, Odessa?
rows.re: Don't tell me you're mixed up / with the terrorists, Odessa?
rows.speaker: suspicious NPC

rows.en: @And, no, I'm not mistaken!
rows.jp: 「見間違いなんかじゃないッ！
rows.lit: I know what I saw!
rows.re: I know what I saw!
rows.speaker: suspicious NPC

rows.en: @I won't say who, but I'm sure there is a traitor in your group. Be careful.
rows.jp: 「悪いことは言わない / あんたらの中に裏切り者がいる / 気をつけたほうがいい<b:8a8f>地の人間が / スレイハイム解放戦役を生き抜けたのは / 誰もが手を取り、あきらめなかったからだ
rows.lit: Take my word for it: there's a traitor among you; you'd best beware.
rows.re: Take my word for it: there's a / traitor among you. You'd best / beware.
rows.speaker: suspicious NPC

rows.en: @If the people of Filgaia would pull together like that, we could make it through this peril.
rows.jp: 「もしも、ファルガイア中の人間が / 同方に手を取り、あきらめなかったとすれば / この異世事態、切り抜けられるのかもな<b:8a90>作の危機〜 / 逃げる場所なんて、どこにもない
rows.lit: If everyone in Filgaia joined hands the same way and refused to give up, we might yet weather this calamity.
rows.re: If everyone in Filgaia joined / hands and refused to give up, we / might weather this calamity.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But that doesn't mean we should just give up.
rows.jp: 「だからといって / すべてを<88ab>げ出すつもりはない
rows.lit: That said, I've no intention of throwing it all away.
rows.re: That said, I've no intention of / throwing it all away.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @The people of Slayheim have beat the odds before.
rows.jp: 「私たち、スレイハイムの民は / かつて<b:8a59><b:8a91>を<b:8a92>り<b:8a93>えてきたんだ
rows.lit: We, the people of Slayheim, have overcome despair before.
rows.re: We, the people of Slayheim, have / overcome despair before.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @And we can do it again.
rows.jp: 「今度も右け止めてみせるだけだ
rows.lit: We'll simply weather this one too.
rows.re: We'll simply weather this one / too.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But how long can we stand up to something that devours the sky itself?
rows.jp: 「だが、空を失うといった / <b:8a94>無的な<b:8a73><889b>に対して / どこまで<b:8a95>えるのだろうか？
rows.lit: But against a nihilistic calamity like losing the sky, how long can we hold?
rows.re: But against a nihilistic calamity / like losing the sky, how long can / we hold?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I don't know the answer to that one.
rows.jp: 「私には / わかりかねるな<b:8a96><b:8a97>〜
rows.lit: That, I could not say.
rows.re: That, I could not say.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Vinsfeld made a deal with Slayheim, they say.
rows.jp: 「ヴィンスフェルトは / スレイハイム国と / 取り招きを交わそうとしたという
rows.lit: Vinsfeld, they say, sought to strike a bargain with the Slayheim state.
rows.re: Vinsfeld, they say, sought to / strike a bargain with the / Slayheim state.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @In exchange for shutting down the resistance, he schemed to acquire wealth and power.
rows.jp: 「レジスタンス活動の<8996>止と招き<88fb>えに / <b:8a99>と<88b2>力をつかもうと / <b:8a9a>案したそうだ
rows.lit: In exchange for halting the resistance, he schemed to seize wealth and power, so it's said.
rows.re: In exchange for halting the / resistance, he schemed to seize / wealth and power.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But that wasn't what the people who joined the Liberation Army were risking their lives for.
rows.jp: 「そんなつもりのために / 解放軍に参加した民衆たちは / 命を<b:8a9d>したわけではない
rows.lit: The common folk who joined the Liberation Army did not risk their lives for ends like those.
rows.re: The common folk who joined the / Liberation Army did not risk / their lives for ends like those.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Naturally, there was a great backlash, and support for Vinsfeld plummeted.
rows.jp: 「当部、大きく反発され / その時を<b:8a9e>にヴィンスフェルトの<b:8a9f>持は / 辺降<b:8aa0>の一<b:8aa1>をたどったらしい
rows.lit: Naturally there was great backlash, and from that moment Vinsfeld's support only slid downhill.
rows.re: Naturally there was great / backlash, and from that moment / Vinsfeld's support slid downhill.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @That backlash must have been what drove Vinsfeld to sell out the Liberation Army.
rows.jp: 「その時の確<b:8aa2>が / 後に解放軍を売り渡すなどという / <b:8aa4><b:8a86>につながったんだろうな軍といえば / あの街戦の立役者〜 / <b:8a6a>々しいイメージがつきものだ
rows.lit: The rancor of that time likely led to the outrage of later selling out the Liberation Army.
rows.re: The rancor of that time likely / led to the outrage of later / selling out the Army.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But what happened to them after the war was tragic.
rows.jp: 「だが、その最後は / あまりにも悲<b:8aa5>であったと
rows.lit: But their end, they say, was tragic beyond measure.
rows.re: But their end, they say, was / tragic beyond measure.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Their leader, Vinsfeld, sought to use the Liberation Army for his own personal gain, some say.
rows.jp: 「リーダーのヴィンスフェルトは / 私的な目<b:8aa6>見のために解放軍を利用しようと / たくらんでいたというではないか
rows.lit: Their leader Vinsfeld, they say, schemed to use the Liberation Army for his own private gain.
rows.re: Their leader Vinsfeld, they say, / schemed to use the Liberation / Army for private gain.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Some say he sold out the Liberation Army to avoid being condemned as a war criminal along with the rest.
rows.jp: 「それどころか / 戦後、戦犯として自身の立場が危うくなると / 保身のために解放軍を売ったとも〜
rows.lit: Worse: when his own standing as a war criminal grew perilous after the war, he sold the Army to save himself.
rows.re: Worse: when his standing grew / perilous after the war, he sold / the Army to save himself.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Who knows what Vinsfeld really did, or why he did it.
rows.jp: 「<b:8a3b>られる事実と / <b:8a3b>られない真実〜
rows.lit: The facts that are told, and the truth that is not.
rows.re: The facts that are told, and the / truth that is not.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @The same goes for the Slayheim Liberation War.
rows.jp: 「スレイハイムの戦いもまた / 部りなのだ〜悲<b:8a61>の / 終結だったのだろうか？
rows.lit: The battle of Slayheim, too, is but one part of it.
rows.re: The battle of Slayheim, too, is / but one part of it.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @The Victorias were moderates, but were executed on the grounds they collaborated with the king.
rows.jp: 「スレイハイムの国<b:8aa7>に異を<b:8aa8>えていた / 穏健派一家ヴィクトリア<b:8a3c>は / 王に連なるものとして処断されたという
rows.lit: The moderate house of Victoria, who dissented from Slayheim's policy, were executed as kin to the king.
rows.re: The moderate house of Victoria, / who dissented from state policy, / were executed as king's kin.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Only one escaped the guillotine, a young daughter who fled filled with hatred for the Liberation Army.
rows.jp: 「当<b:8aa9>は断<b:8aaa><b:8aab>の<b:8aac>と消え / 数幼いひとり娘は解放軍を<b:8aad>みながら / 行方をくらませたと聞いている
rows.lit: The house vanished to the guillotine, and the young only daughter, hating the Liberation Army, disappeared.
rows.re: The house fell to the guillotine, / and the young only daughter, / hating the Army, disappeared.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Sadness begets sadness, they say. That's just what happened, don't you think?
rows.jp: 「悲しみは / 悲しみを呼ぶと言うが / まさにその言葉通りだと思わないか？<b:8a89>に隠された / <88bf>大建<b:8aae>物があるとのウワサだ
rows.lit: Sorrow calls to sorrow, they say; is this not exactly that?
rows.re: Sorrow calls to sorrow, they say. / Is this not exactly that?
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @That may have something to do with that shady group that bought up all those supplies in town.
rows.jp: 「あやしい一団がこの場から / 大<886f>の物資を搬出していたとの話と / 何か関係あるのかもしれぬ
rows.lit: It may have some link to the tale of a shady band hauling masses of supplies from this town.
rows.re: It may have some link to the tale / of a shady band hauling supplies / from this town.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Maybe they were the ones everyone's making such a fuss about -- Odessa!
rows.jp: 「もしや、あの一団こそが / <b:8ab0>を発がすオデッサなる<b:8ab1>だろうか？
rows.lit: Could that band be the very Odessa that has the world astir?
rows.re: Could that band be the very / Odessa that has the world astir?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @You're with the group that took supplies into the desert, right? I remember your sharp eyes.
rows.jp: 「そうだ、先の<88db>の道に物資を運んでいた / あの連中の仲間だろ？ / その<b:8ab2>い目、忘れはしないぞ
rows.lit: That's right: you're with the lot that hauled supplies to the desert yonder, aren't you? I don't forget those sharp eyes.
rows.re: You're with the lot that hauled / supplies to the desert, aren't / you? I don't forget those eyes.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @So how come you're not with them today?
rows.jp: 「だが、今回はなぜ / 連中と行動を<b:8ab3>にしていないのだ<b:8ab4>いるヴィンスフェルトなる悪党 / あいつは元・スレイハイム解放軍の / リーダーであったという
rows.lit: But why aren't you with them this time?
rows.re: But why aren't you with them this / time?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Maybe Odessa is just a bunch of Liberation Army troops who were down on their luck after the war.
rows.jp: 「ならば、行き場を失った / スレイハイム解放軍の残<b:8ab6>が / オデッサなのだろうか？<b:8ab7>の<b:8ab8>は / 遠<b:8ab9>させてもらいたいものだよ英雄』のような / 存在の人間がでてきてさ / さっさと空を元に戻してくれないかねぇ
rows.lit: Then could Odessa be the remnants of the Slayheim Liberation Army, left with nowhere to go?
rows.re: Then could Odessa be the remnants / of the Liberation Army, left with / nowhere to go?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Why such a stern look, young man? Did I offend you? What? That's how you normally look? Oh...
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>ん？ / お<b:8abc>さん、恐い探してどうしたんだい？ / あぁ、元からだったかねぇ英雄』のような / 存在の人間がでてきてさ / さっさと空を元に戻してくれないかねぇ英雄』が / 必要なんじゃないかね英雄の名前は知ってるけど / 実<89d2>には見たことないのよ
rows.lit: Hm? What's with the scary face, young man? Oh; it was always like that, was it.
rows.re: Hm? What's with the scary face, / young man? Oh; it was always like / that, was it.
rows.speaker: old woman

rows.en: @People exaggerate, but I'm still sure his exploits are beyond what the average person can do.
rows.jp: 「まぁ、英雄話に<b:8abd><b:8abe>はつきものだけど / でも世人では考えられないほどの / 戦<b:8abf>をあげたに違いないわ英雄の名前は知ってるけど / 実<89d2>には見たことないのよ
rows.lit: Well, hero tales always come embroidered; still, his deeds must have been beyond any common man.
rows.re: Well, hero tales always come / embroidered. Still, his deeds / were beyond any common man.
rows.speaker: old woman

rows.en: @Maybe that's how it is with heroes, but I still wish I could have seen him just once.
rows.jp: 「英雄なんて / 得てしてそんなものなのかねぇ / 一度くらいは見たかった気がするね<b:8ac0><b:8ac1> / そういったものが必要なのかねぇ
rows.lit: Maybe that's just how heroes are; still, I'd have liked to see him once.
rows.re: Maybe that's just how heroes are. / Still, I'd have liked to see him / once.
rows.speaker: old woman

rows.en: @The Slayheim Liberation Army had some hero named 1 as its symbol, right?
rows.jp: 「スレイハイムの解放軍の<b:8ac0><b:8ac1>は / [05]おとかいう / 英雄だったっていう話しだけどね軍には[05]おっていう / 英雄がいたらしいけど〜〜
rows.lit: The Slayheim Liberation Army's figurehead was some hero called {1}, so the story goes.
rows.re: The Liberation Army's figurehead / was some hero called {1}, so the / story goes.
rows.speaker: old woman

rows.en: @One person can't change the course of a war, right? Isn't is strange how things get exaggerated?
rows.jp: 「戦争って、一人の英雄の力で / どうにかなるものなのかしらねぇ / 話しが<b:8abd><b:8abe>されてるんじゃないのかい？軍にとっては / 悲しい<b:8ac2>利でしかないだろうね
rows.lit: Can one hero's strength really turn a war? Isn't the story just embroidered?
rows.re: Can one hero's strength really / turn a war? Isn't the story just / embroidered?
rows.speaker: old woman

rows.en: @What did they fight for? What did they die for? They died in vain, if you ask me.
rows.jp: 「なんのために戦い / なんのために死んでいったのか / 無<b:8ac3>に命を<b:8ac4>らしただけじゃない塩となったスレイハイム / それを見るたびに / 人の<b:8ac5>かさを信じてしまうねぇ
rows.lit: What did they fight for, what did they die for? They only spent their lives for nothing.
rows.re: What did they fight for, what did / they die for? They only spent / their lives for nothing.
rows.speaker: cynic

rows.en: @Why did things have to go that far? How foolish people are.
rows.jp: 「なんであそこまで / しなきゃならいのかねぇ / 本当に、<b:8ac5>かしいことだね<b:8ac6>う<b:8ac6>う<b:8a7c><b:8ac6>わない英雄の出現を / 待っているだけの<b:8ac7>期なんて / もう無いのかもしれない
rows.lit: Why did it have to go that far? Truly a foolish business.
rows.re: Why did it have to go that far? / Truly a foolish business.
rows.speaker: cynic

rows.en: @We have to figure out what we ordinary people can do right now.
rows.jp: 「だとすれば / 英雄ではない僕たちができることを / 今回にでも見つけなければならないな英雄の<b:8ac8><b:8a55>を<b:8a91>んでいるとしたら / それは都合のいい考えではないだろうか？恐れを<b:8ac9>じ得ない〜
rows.lit: In that case, we who are no heroes must find what we can do, and find it now.
rows.re: In that case, we who are no / heroes must find what we can do, / and find it now.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But people don't seem to be worried to the point of taking action.
rows.jp: 「だが、どこか緊<b:8abe>信が / 欠けているようにも思われるのだ
rows.lit: And yet a certain urgency seems to be missing somewhere.
rows.re: And yet a certain urgency seems / to be missing somewhere.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Maybe they're all waiting for a hero to appear, like during the civil war 5 years ago.
rows.jp: 「５数前の街戦のように / 誰もが英雄の出現を / <b:8a91>んでいるのではなかろうか<b:8aca><b:8abf>は / 特り知れないだろう
rows.lit: Perhaps, as in the civil war five years back, everyone is wishing for a hero to appear.
rows.re: Perhaps, as in the civil war five / years back, everyone is wishing / for a hero to appear.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But that's not the real reason he deserves to be called a hero.
rows.jp: 「だが、真に[05]おを / 英雄と呼ばしめる理由は / そこではないのだ
rows.lit: But the true reason {1} deserves the name of hero is not that.
rows.re: But the true reason {1} deserves / the name of hero is not that.
rows.speaker: veteran

rows.en: @He is a hero because he sacrificed himself to protect his war buddies after they were sold out.
rows.jp: 「あの<b:8acb><b:8acc>党によって売られた解放軍同胞を / <b:8ace>が身を<b:8acf><b:8ad0>にして<b:8ad1>り抜いたところこそ / 彼を英雄たらしめているのだ<b:8a96><b:8a97>〜 / 生死不次とも報じられた / 英雄[05]お・エヴァンス〜
rows.lit: It is that he shielded his sold-out Army comrades at the cost of his own body; that is what makes him a hero.
rows.re: He shielded his sold-out Army / comrades at the cost of his own / body. That makes him a hero.
rows.speaker: veteran

rows.en: @But he reappeared and used himself as bait to save a group of his comrades from their pursuers.
rows.jp: 「でも、彼は、<b:8ac8>び<b:8a43>を現わすと / 追跡部隊から同胞の目をそらすため / <b:8ad2>の役をかって出たんだ
rows.lit: But when he showed himself again, he volunteered as the decoy to draw the pursuers' eyes from his comrades.
rows.re: When he showed himself again, he / volunteered as decoy to draw the / pursuers from his comrades.
rows.speaker: veteran

rows.en: @Naturally, the pursuers went after 1 because they thought a |hero| would be more valuable.
rows.jp: 「英雄の名前には<b:8ad3><8875>があるから / 追っ手はこぞって / [05]おをねらったという
rows.lit: A hero's name carries a price, so the pursuers all went after {1}, they say.
rows.re: A hero's name carries a price, so / the pursuers all went after {1}, / they say.
rows.speaker: veteran

rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @What wonderful creatures the Dragons are! Dead or alive, they benefit us!
rows.jp: 「しかし、ドラゴンとは良い生き物だな / 死んでいても生きていても / ワシに利<b:8a91>をもたらしてくれるッ
rows.lit: But Dragons are fine creatures: dead or alive, they bring me profit!
rows.re: But Dragons are fine creatures. / Dead or alive, they bring me / profit!
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @Haw haw haw!
rows.jp: 「がっはっはっはっ〜<b:8b0b>[14][10]ヌ[01]<f089>[06]ギルドグラードマスター / 「なんだ？ / 先の核ドラゴンを<b:8a92><b:8a93>したことか？
rows.lit: Gwa ha ha ha!
rows.re: Gwa ha ha ha!
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @We merely reaped what we had sown. There is no reason to thank us.
rows.jp: 「ワシは、自分のまいた種を / 自分で<b:8a95>ろうとしたまでのコト / 単にお前たちに礼を言われる<b:8a96>合いはないぞ
rows.lit: I merely tried to reap the seeds I myself had sown; no cause for you to thank me.
rows.re: I merely tried to reap the seeds / I myself had sown. No cause for / you to thank me.
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @It is I who should thank you. I apologize for the trouble we caused.
rows.jp: 「礼ならこちらが言わせてもらおう / <f040><f041><f042>手間かけさせてすまなかったな<b:8b0b>[14][10]ニ[01]ｊ[06]ギルドグラードマスター / 「あの、核ドラゴン / グラウスヴァインをどうにかしないとな
rows.lit: The thanks should be mine to give; sorry for the trouble we caused you.
rows.re: The thanks should be mine to / give. Sorry for the trouble we / caused you.
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @I hope I am not pushing my luck, but we need your help.
rows.jp: 「今更、ムシのいい話しだが / お前たちの力を<b:8a97>してほしい
rows.lit: It's brazen of me to ask now, but I need you to lend us your strength.
rows.re: It's brazen of me to ask now, but / I need you to lend us your / strength.
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @Of course, we will assist you in any way we can. Please help us!
rows.jp: 「もちろん / ワシらもできるだけのコトはするつもりだ / すまないが頼むぞ<b:8b0b>[14][10]か[01][f5]眠ギルドグラードマスター / 「ダメだッ！ ダメだッ！
rows.lit: Of course, we mean to do everything we can as well; sorry, but I'm counting on you.
rows.re: Of course, we mean to do all we / can as well. Sorry, but I'm / counting on you.
rows.speaker: Master

rows.en: @How do we fight Odessa now that they possess both |Heimdal Gazzo| AND the nuclear weapon?
rows.jp: 「『ヘイムダル・ガッツォー』に『核』ッ！ / この２つの<b:8a98>っているオデッサと / どう戦えというんだッ！<b:8b06>ギルドグラードマスター / 「まさか『核』を<b:8a99>われるとはな〜
rows.lit: "Heimdal Gazzo" AND the nuke! How are we to fight an Odessa holding both of these?!
rows.re: |Heimdal Gazzo| AND the nuke! How / are we to fight an Odessa holding / both of these?!
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.en: @But how on earth did Odessa know the nuke was on that train?
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>しかし、なぜオデッサは / 『核』を<89dc>陸に<b:8a9a>んでいることを / 知っていたんだ？
rows.lit: But how did Odessa know the nuke was being carried on that train?
rows.re: But how did Odessa know the nuke / was being carried on that train?
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.en: @Could there be a spy in our midst?
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>スパイでもいるというのかッ！<b:8b06>「さすがに、暗い空がこんなに続くと / 人々の心も暗くなってしまうようですね / 以前は、あんなに<b:8a9b>やかだった場が〜<b:8a75>み』のようなものを / 信じたのだが〜 私だけかな〜？
rows.lit: Are you saying there's a spy?!
rows.re: Are you saying there's a spy?!
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.en: @I wouldn't blame the dragon for being mad. After all, we process dragon fossils into fuel.
rows.jp: 「ま、我々はドラゴンの遺跡を概<b:8a67>して / <b:8a8c>料にしているのだから / それも当たり前か〜<b:8a9c>書<b:8a9d>のじいさんが / <b:8a9e>い探をしていたが / 何か<b:8a9f>み事でもあるのかな？
rows.lit: Well, we refine Dragon remains into fuel, so I suppose that's only natural.
rows.re: Well, we refine Dragon remains / into fuel, so I suppose that's / only natural.
rows.speaker: engineer

rows.en: @Oh, well. Who can blame him with the sky the way it is?
rows.jp: 「ま、空がこんなになっちゃ / 気持ちも分からんではないが<b:8a42><b:8a5b>は / かなり高いようだな魔次の遺跡を / 左<b:8a3b>したものだったそうだ<b:8aa0>がいたらオレの所に連れてこい
rows.lit: Well, with the sky like this, I can't say I don't understand the feeling.
rows.re: Well, with the sky like this, I / can't say I don't understand the / feeling.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I'll teach that hypocrite a lesson he'll never forget!
rows.jp: 「そんな<b:8aa1><b:8aa2><b:8aa3><b:8aa4>には / オレがヤキをいれてやるぜッ！<b:8aa5>』がもたらすモノの中にはな / 『<b:8a42><b:8a5b>の急<8a04>な進歩』もあるってコトを / 忘れるなッ！核』を使いやがるなんて / オレたちを道連れって<b:8aa6>かよッ！核なんか使ったら世界征服する / ファルガイアがなくなっちまうってのに
rows.lit: I'll give that two-faced so-and-so a lesson myself!
rows.re: I'll give that two-faced / so-and-so a lesson myself!
rows.speaker: hothead

rows.en: @Perhaps conquering the world was never their goal.
rows.jp: 「ホントに世界征服する気が / あるのかね<b:8aa9><b:8aaa>』が / 帰らなかったらしいな
rows.lit: Did they ever really mean to conquer the world, I wonder?
rows.re: Did they ever really mean to / conquer the world, I wonder?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But perhaps you were fortunate to destroy Odessa's base with the loss of only one life.
rows.jp: 「だが、たった一人の<b:8aab><b:8aac>で / <88e6>帯一つを<b:8aad>せたんだから / それはそれで、スゲェことだぜ<b:8a40>て辺さいました
rows.lit: Still, to bring down a whole base at the cost of a single casualty; that's something, in its way.
rows.re: Still, to bring down a whole base / at the cost of one casualty. / That's something.
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.en: @I have created Full Clip, a device that transfers the user's telepathic strength to an ARM.
rows.jp: 「ドラゴンの生体サンプルの解<b:8aae>によって / 使用者の概<b:8a76>力をアームに付<b:8aaf>する / 『フルフラット』が完成したのです
rows.lit: By analyzing the Dragon's living sample, I completed "Full Clip," which imparts the user's willpower to an ARM.
rows.re: By analyzing the Dragon's living / sample, I completed |Full Clip|: / it feeds your will to an ARM.
rows.speaker: scientist

rows.en: @It is somewhat difficult to control, but I am sure you could handle it, 0.
rows.jp: 「まだ、制<89c7>が<b:8ab0>しいですが / [05]ぉさんなら / 使いこなせると思います
rows.lit: Control is still difficult, but I believe you, {1}, could master it.
rows.re: Control is still difficult, but I / believe you, {1}, could master / it.
rows.speaker: scientist

rows.en: @One thing to keep in mind is that it discharges every round in your ARM when activated.
rows.jp: 「<88f7>意帯としては / 発動するとアームの全<b:8a43>を発<b:8ab1>し<b:8ab2>くして / しまうこと
rows.lit: One caution: on activation it fires off every round in the ARM.
rows.re: One caution: on activation it / fires off every round in the ARM.
rows.speaker: scientist

rows.en: @Also, how powerful it is depends on your ARM's remaining ammo count when you equip it. Here, take it!
rows.jp: 「また、アームの残<b:8ab3>年によって / 威力が変合します / どうぞ、<b:8ab4>けとってください<b:8a87>得した父上は、機<b:8ab6>がいいと / つい調家に<b:8a8f>ってしまいがちなのです
rows.lit: Its power also varies with the ARM's remaining ammo; please, take it.
rows.re: Its power also varies with the / ARM's remaining ammo. Please, / take it.
rows.speaker: scientist

rows.en: @Please forgive him if he takes a joke a little too far.
rows.jp: 「<b:8ab7><b:8ab8>が過ぎるコトがありますが / どうか、大目に見てやってください〜〜
rows.lit: His jokes sometimes go too far; please be forgiving of him.
rows.re: His jokes sometimes go too far. / Please be forgiving of him.
rows.speaker: aide

rows.en: @Please use it in the fight to save Filgaia!
rows.jp: 「少しでもファルガイアの為に / 役立ってくれたらうれしいです
rows.lit: I would be glad if it serves Filgaia even a little.
rows.re: I would be glad if it serves / Filgaia even a little.
rows.speaker: Master's son

rows.en: @The recent events seem to have changed my father, too.
rows.jp: 「今回の件で / 父上も少し変わったような気がします
rows.lit: I feel this affair has changed my father a little, too.
rows.re: I feel this affair has changed my / father a little, too.
rows.speaker: Master's son

rows.en: @The recent events seem to have changed my father, too.
rows.jp: 「今回の件で / 父上も少し変わったような気がします
rows.lit: I feel this affair has changed my father a little, too.
rows.re: I feel this affair has changed my / father a little, too.
rows.speaker: Master's son

rows.en: @would solve everything and bring peace back to Filgaia.
rows.jp: 「ファルガイアに<b:8a85><b:8a86>が戻ると / そう、信じていたのに〜
rows.lit: I truly believed peace would return to Filgaia...
rows.re: I truly believed peace would / return to Filgaia...
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I can't help thinking that the black sky is a curse that Odessa put on us.
rows.jp: 「この暗い空〜 / まるで、オデッサの<b:8ab9>念を表わしている〜 / そのように信じずには、いられません〜<b:8aba>通りに / なってしまうのでしょうか〜
rows.lit: This dark sky, as if it embodies Odessa's lingering malice; I cannot help but believe it.
rows.re: This dark sky, as if it embodies / Odessa's lingering malice. I / cannot help but believe it.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I apologize for keeping the nuke a secret. I did not know myself, but I feel as if I deceived you.
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>それから『核』のコトですが〜 / わたくしも知らなかったコトとはいえ / <88fc>してしまったみたいですみませんでした〜<b:8a9e>い空には戻らない / 何が原因なのか、どうすれば戻るのか / そして、<b:8a81>の<b:8a81>実を知るものはいるのか？
rows.lit: And as for the nuke: though I did not know myself, it seems I deceived you, and I am sorry.
rows.re: And as for the nuke: though I did / not know myself, it seems I / deceived you. I am sorry.
rows.speaker: Master's son

rows.en: @Wait a minute. |Real truth| ... Does that make sense? Ah, forget it.
rows.jp: 「〜ん？ / 今、変な魔法の使い方をしたような〜？ / まあ、いいか<b:8a9c>書<b:8a9d>のおじいさんなら知ってるかもよ
rows.lit: Hm? Did I just use magic in some odd way? Ah, never mind.
rows.re: Hm? Did I just use magic in some / odd way? Ah, never mind.
rows.speaker: library worker

rows.en: @He's the Lord of the Library.
rows.jp: 「なんたって、<b:8a9c>書<b:8a9d>の<b:8abb>だからね核ドラゴン攻撃<b:8a83>ぎの時 / なぜかギルドグラードマスターが / やる気全開だったんだ〜
rows.lit: He is, after all, the lord of the library.
rows.re: He is, after all, the lord of the / library.
rows.speaker: library worker

rows.en: @I am SO overworked! Man, my head STILL aches... or is it |hurts|? Which do you think is better?
rows.jp: 「おかげで、俺はコキ使われちゃったよ〜 / ああ、<b:8abc><b:8abd>が<b:8abd>いよ〜〜〜ん？ / 今、変な魔法の使い方をしたような〜？<b:8abe>する<b:8abe>が多くなってね
rows.lit: Thanks to that I've been worked to the bone; oh, my head aches... hm? Did I just use magic oddly?
rows.re: I've been worked to the bone. Oh, / my head aches... hm? Did I just / use magic oddly?
rows.speaker: library worker

rows.en: @One store gave me a going-out-of- business gift. Hey... That doesn't make sense, does it?
rows.jp: 「そこで、閉<b:8abe>渡念の『<b:8abf><b:8ac0><8a0c>品』を / プレゼントされたんだ / でも、変な魔法の使い方をしたような〜？<b:8ab6>になるのも / 仕方ないですね〜<b:8a3c>の行<8815>人たちが<89e6>していたのですが / なんでも、オデッサは渓谷場を / <89d0>っているとかいないとか〜
rows.lit: There I was given a "closing-sale keepsake" as a present; but did I just use magic oddly?
rows.re: There I was given a closing-sale / keepsake as a present. But did I / just use magic oddly?
rows.speaker: library worker

rows.en: @I have learned to be grateful when everyone makes it through another day alive and safe.
rows.jp: 「それは、『みんなが今回も無事だった』〜 / <b:8ac1><b:8ab3>は、全部気にも止めなかった事ですが / とっても、大切なコトだったんですね<b:8ac2>りが、まだまだ弱いのでしょうか〜？<b:8a76>よ、どうか世界をお救い辺さい〜
rows.lit: It's that "everyone made it through today safe" — before, I never gave it a thought, but it was precious all along.
rows.re: "Everyone made it through today / safe." I never gave it a thought / before, but it was precious.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @To the 1southeast0 is an island that resembles a coiled snake. They say energy collects there.
rows.jp: 「そういえば、ココから[11]お先側[11]ぉに / ヘビがとぐろを<8812>いた方な他があるんじゃが / そこには、地<89f4>が集まっているそうじゃ
rows.lit: Come to think of it, off yonder is an isle like a coiled snake; they say the earth's energy gathers there.
rows.re: Come to think of it, |off yonder| / is an isle like a coiled snake. / Energy gathers there.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @That might be a Raypoint.
rows.jp: 「そこがレイポイントかもしれんぞい
rows.lit: That may well be a Raypoint.
rows.re: That may well be a Raypoint.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @inaccessible place -- like the crater of a volcano, for instance.
rows.jp: 「人の手が入りにくい所が可能性が高いの / <8943>えば、枯谷の枯口とかじゃな〜核ドラゴン』じゃが / 古代魔次時に作られた / 『同時』らしいのじゃ
rows.lit: Places hard for human hands to reach are likeliest; say, a volcano's crater.
rows.re: Places hard for human hands to / reach are likeliest. Say, a / volcano's crater.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @The ancient texts say experiments were held. Maybe they are what led to ancient civilization's collapse.
rows.jp: 「何回かの同時実験をしていた / 渡記も残っておる / それが破滅への<b:8a93>だったのかもしれんの〜核』の / 落辺地帯を調べておるんじゃが〜
rows.lit: Records remain of several experiments; perhaps those were the road to their ruin.
rows.re: Records remain of several / experiments. Perhaps those were / the road to their ruin.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @It looks like it's... Oh, these calculations must be wrong. I HOPE they are wrong!
rows.jp: 「もしかしたら〜 / いや、ワシの特<b:8ac3>違いじゃろ〜 / そう、間違いであってほしいの〜
rows.lit: Could it be... no, surely my calculations are wrong; yes, I hope they are wrong.
rows.re: Could it be... no, surely my / calculations are wrong. Yes, I / hope they are wrong.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @There are 4 altogether. This one is located 1beyond the mountain southwest of Guild Galad0.
rows.jp: 「４鍵のうちの１鍵が / [11]おギルドグラードから先東の谷を<b:8ac4>えた岸り[11]ぉに / あることが分かったんじゃ
rows.lit: We've learned that one of the four keys lies beyond the valley yonder-east of Guild Galad.
rows.re: We've learned one of the four / keys lies |beyond the valley / yonder-east| of Guild Galad.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @I'll tell that young lady operator at Valeria Chateau!
rows.jp: 「このことは、ヴァレリアシャトーの / オペレーターお<b:8ac5>ちゃんにも伝えとくぞい<b:8a9c>書<b:8a9d>の<b:8ac6>理者じゃ / 口の悪い連中は / 『<b:8a9c>書<b:8a9d>の<b:8abb>』と呼ぶがの<b:8ac7>まったわ / 私もね単れてから彼の存在の大きさを / <b:8ac8>確認しちゃったし〜<f044>
rows.lit: I'll pass this along to the operator lass at Valeria Chateau as well.
rows.re: I'll pass this along to the / operator lass at Valeria Chateau / as well.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @I'm waiting for him now. But what could be keeping him? He'd better not stand me up like last time!
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>あっと / 私がこんなこと言ってたなんて街<b:8ac9>だよ<f044> / 〜でも<8a0d>いなぁ、まだ<b:8aca>りてないのかな〜<b:8a40>てくれたのよ / フッた私を心配してくれるなんて〜<f044>
rows.lit: Oh! Keep it secret that I said any of this. But he's late; hasn't he come down yet?
rows.re: Oh! Keep it secret that I said / any of this. But he's late. / Hasn't he come down yet?
rows.speaker: waiting girl

rows.en: @Afterwards, he said he was sorry, but then he ran away.
rows.jp: 「その後、謝ってきたんだけど〜 / <b:8acb>って逃げちゃったの
rows.lit: Afterward he came to apologize, but then he panicked and ran off.
rows.re: Afterward he came to apologize, / but then he panicked and ran off.
rows.speaker: waiting girl

rows.en: @I should have forgave him then and there, but my foolish pride wouldn't let me.
rows.jp: 「その場で許しても良かったんだけど / こっちから謝りたかったから〜<f044> / <f040><f041><f042>私って、意地っ<b:8acc>りかもね？
rows.lit: I could have forgiven him then and there, but I wanted to apologize first myself; stubborn of me, maybe?
rows.re: I could have forgiven him then, / but I wanted to apologize first / myself. Stubborn, maybe?
rows.speaker: waiting girl

rows.en: @Sigh! My heart is as dark as the sky above!
rows.jp: 「<f040><f041><f042>あぁ〜 / あの暗い空は / 私の心<b:8acd>を表わしているようだわ〜<f05a><b:8ace>違いしてたのよ / まったく、どこか抜けてるんだから
rows.lit: Ahh, that dark sky is like a mirror of my own heart.
rows.re: Ahh, that dark sky is like a / mirror of my own heart.
rows.speaker: waiting girl

rows.en: @But that's part of his charm. Hey, he's late again today, too!
rows.jp: 「でも、そこがいいところなのかもね〜<f044> / <f040><f041><f042>にしても<8a0d>いわねぇ<b:8acf>重の時間になっても<b:8a40>ないのよねぇ〜 / まったく、何をしてるのかしらッ<f059><b:8a64><b:8ad0>人間の僕としては / 空がずっと暗くても / 信信的にそんなに変わらないよ<b:8ad1><b:8ad2>の家を<b:8ad3>らすように / 逃げて行ったのがよく見れたよ<f04a>
rows.lit: But maybe that's his charm; still, he IS late.
rows.re: But maybe that's his charm. / Still, he IS late.
rows.speaker: waiting girl

rows.en: @And then I high-tailed it out of there, too!
rows.jp: 「まぁ、その後 / オレも急いで逃げたけどね〜<b:8a38>気は、それほど変わってないよ / こんな時だからこそ、元気を出さなくちゃな
rows.lit: Well, after that I beat a quick retreat myself.
rows.re: Well, after that I beat a quick / retreat myself.
rows.speaker: storyteller

rows.en: @Of course, I could do without those Odessa guys.
rows.jp: 「でも、オデッサみたいな<b:8ad4>は / <b:8ace><b:8ad5>してほしいよ<b:8a82>多な信じがするだろ？ / でも、オレはそこが<b:8a4c>きなんだ<b:8a55>時が必要になるコトもあるだろう
rows.lit: But the likes of Odessa, I'd like to see wiped away for good.
rows.re: But the likes of Odessa, I'd like / to see wiped away for good.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @But we have to use them carefully to avoid ending up like Slayheim.
rows.jp: 「だが、使い方を<b:8ad6>り / スレイハイムのニの<b:8ad7>だけには / ならないようにな<b:8a7c>は、今は亡きスレイハイムと / <b:8a55>時などの開発を<b:8ad8>っていたものだ
rows.lit: But mind how we use them, lest we become a second Slayheim.
rows.re: But mind how we use them, lest we / become a second Slayheim.
rows.speaker: engineer

rows.en: @Technological progress was a lot faster in those days.
rows.jp: 「やはり、<b:8ad8>い合っていた頃の方が / <b:8a42><b:8a5b>の進歩が早かったな<b:8a55>時の<b:8ad9><b:8a45>を命じたらしい〜
rows.speaker: SKIPPED - no content box in decode

rows.en: @Who does he intend to fight?
rows.jp: 「一体、何と戦うつもりなのだ？<b:8a55>時は、使い方によって / 人々の脅威にも / 愛する人を<b:8ada>ることもできる
rows.lit: Just what does he mean to fight?
rows.re: Just what does he mean to fight?
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @IF used properly, that is.
rows.jp: 「使い方を間違えないことだ<b:8a55>時なども / ギルドグラード<b:8a67>のモノが / 結構あるはずだ謝ってきて / 許してくれたよ<f04a> / 俺が謝った時の<b:8adb>意が伝わったのかな？
rows.lit: The key is not to mistake how it is used.
rows.re: The key is not to mistake how it / is used.
rows.speaker: engineer

rows.en: @Today is our first date since we made up. But she's late. I wonder what's keeping her...
rows.jp: 「今回は / <b:8adc><8865>りしてから押めてのデートなのさ / <f040><f041><f042>でも、彼女<8a0d>いなぁ〜<f04b><b:8a40>た時に / 彼女のコトが心配になって / 行ってみたんだ

rows.re: The operation is a success.

rows.en: @Maybe this life is nothing to be proud of.
rows.jp: 「あんまり<89e5>を<b:8a56>って / 言えるもんじゃないのかもしれないな
rows.lit: Maybe it's not the sort of life a man can brag about.
rows.re: Maybe it's not the sort of life a / man can brag about.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @But it's still a helluva lot better than living in despair, cowering in fear, like a lot of folks.
rows.jp: 「でもな、<b:8a57><b:8a58>にうつむいて / ただ右ちひしがれている連中よりは / ずっと人間らしい生き方をしているつもりだ<b:8a59>えてきてな / <8933>の方はあったかいぜ
rows.lit: But it beats living hunched in despair like those broken folks; more human, the way I see it.
rows.re: But it beats living hunched in / despair like those broken folks; / more human, the way I see it.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @I've noticed that the greedy tend to do alright for themselves, no matter how crazy the world gets.
rows.jp: 「どんな世界であろうと / <b:8a5a><b:8a5b>に生きていこうとするヤツは / けっこう何とかなるもんだぜ<b:8a5c>ぎすぎなんだよ
rows.lit: Whatever the world's like, a fellow bent on living greedily tends to manage well enough.
rows.re: Whatever the world's like, a / fellow bent on living greedily / tends to manage well enough.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @I think this peril is gonna give Mercs like us plenty of opportunities to strike it rich.
rows.jp: 「今度の異世事態〜 / 少なくとも僕たち渡り鳥は / 一<b:8a5d><b:8a5e>金のチャンスとみるね
rows.lit: This crisis; at least we Drifters see it as a chance to strike it rich in one shot.
rows.re: This crisis; at least we Drifters / see it as a chance to strike it / rich in one shot.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @Assuming we stay alive, that is.
rows.jp: 「まあ、命あっての物<b:8a5f>だがな<b:8a41>同だから言えるんだがな / 戦いってのは / 何でもかんでも<b:8a60>うものではないのさ
rows.lit: Well, so long as we stay alive to spend it.
rows.re: Well, so long as we stay alive to / spend it.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @'Cause during the Slayheim Liberation War, we had plenty to eat and plenty of women!
rows.jp: 「少なくとも / スレイハイム解放戦は僕に / オンナとメシを<b:8a61>えてくれたな来 / <b:8a41>同の僕は / おまんまの食い上げだぜ
rows.lit: At the least, the Slayheim liberation war gave me women and food aplenty.
rows.re: At the least, the Slayheim / liberation war gave me women and / food aplenty.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @Now I just manage to scrape out a living as a half-assed Merc.
rows.jp: 「今じゃこうして / 渡り鳥の<b:8a62><8973>事をして / <b:8a63>口をしのいでいるわけさ<b:8a52> / 「世界のどこにも安全な地がないのなら / 私は『<89de><89df>輝』の<89f5>にいます
rows.lit: Now I scrape by doing odd Drifter jobs like this, just getting by.
rows.re: Now I scrape by doing odd Drifter / jobs like this, just getting by.
rows.speaker: Merc

rows.en: @As conductor, it is my duty to protect her to the very end.
rows.jp: 「『<89de><89df>輝』を<b:8a53>り、<b:8a54>に在るのが / 陸<b:8a52>である私の使命です<b:8a52> / 「『<89de><89df>輝』の調備は完了しています / いつでも発陸オーライです鉄道『<89de><89df>輝』に乗りますか？[18]か
rows.lit: To protect the "Dianbai Guang" and see her through to the end is my duty as conductor.
rows.re: To protect the |Dianbai Guang| / and see her through is my duty as / conductor.
rows.speaker: conductor

rows.en: @Perhaps I'm going against his wishes by being bound to the past for so long.
rows.jp: 「だとすれば / いつまでもここで『過<b:8a65>』に<b:8a66>られていては / うちの人に<b:8a67>し<b:8a68>ありませんね
rows.lit: If so, then clinging here to the "past" forever would be a disservice to my husband.
rows.re: If so, then clinging here to the / past forever would be a / disservice to my husband.
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @I know that I should give up hope that my husband will ever come home.
rows.jp: 「私たちはここで / あの人の帰りを / 待つべきではない、と〜
rows.lit: That we should not go on waiting here for him to come home...
rows.re: That we should not go on waiting / here for him to come home...
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @But I can't leave here until I understand why it was he had to fight in that war.
rows.jp: 「でも、うちの人が戦の果てに何を遺したのか / それを見つけるまでは / ここをあとにできないのです〜<b:8a69><b:8a6a>を / <b:8a6b>く<b:8a6c>りつぶすかのように / <b:8a6d><b:8a6e>な<b:8a6f>の原<b:8a70>は広がっています<b:8a71> / 解放<b:8a72>は / <b:8a72><b:8a42><b:8a73>義に<b:8a74>利しました
rows.lit: But until I learn what my husband left behind at the end of that war, I cannot leave this place.
rows.re: But until I learn what my husband / left behind at that war's end, I / cannot leave this place.
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @So many precious lives were lost in the war. The dead lie buried under the salt flats.
rows.jp: 「ですが、年多の帰らない人〜 / 年多の帰らない命が / <b:8a6f>の大地に<898f>んでいるのです<b:8a72>に<b:8a75><b:8a76>して / <b:8a72><b:8a42><b:8a73>義に立ち向かいました
rows.lit: But so many who never returned, so many lost lives, lie sleeping beneath the salt flats.
rows.re: But so many who never returned, / so many lost lives, lie sleeping / beneath the salt flats.
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @The fighting was fierce. He was listed as missing in action.
rows.jp: 「ですが、戦<8945>が<88f1>しさを<b:8a59>す中 / 行方が知れなくなってしまったのです
rows.lit: But as the fighting grew fierce, he went missing.
rows.re: But as the fighting grew fierce, / he went missing.
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @Today, like every other day, my son and I are waiting at the station in the hope my husband will return.
rows.jp: 「今回もこうして<89e2>家と一<b:8a77>に / 人が行き交うステーションで / うちの人の<b:8a78>を<8856>しているのです<b:8a79>さんだって<b:8a58>んではいないよ
rows.lit: Today, too, my child and I wait at the crowded station, searching for my husband's return.
rows.re: Today, too, my child and I wait / at the crowded station, watching / for my husband's return.
rows.speaker: war widow

rows.en: @I finally realized it was my duty to take Father's place and take Mother home.
rows.jp: 「やっとわかったんだ / お<b:8a7a>さんを<b:8a43>へ帰すのは / お<b:8a79>さんじゃない、俺の役目だって<b:8a79>さん、帰ってこないんだ / もう、帰ってこないかもしれない
rows.lit: I finally understood: taking Mother home isn't Father's job, it's mine.
rows.re: I finally understood: taking / Mother home isn't Father's job, / it's mine.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @that Father will probably never come home. Ever.
rows.jp: 「<b:8a7b>いているお<b:8a7a>さんを見ていると / 時々、そう思うことがあるんだ<b:8b7c>[06]「<b:8a7c>いお空〜 / どこかへ行っちゃったみたいだ
rows.lit: Watching Mother cry, sometimes I think that.
rows.re: Watching Mother cry, sometimes I / think that.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @But I know it will be back. Just like Father will be back some day.
rows.jp: 「でも、きっと帰ってくるよね？ / 俺のお<b:8a79>さんといっしょに<b:8a79>さんが戦<b:8a64>に行ったのは / 俺がずっと小さな頃〜 / だから、探はおぼえていないんだ
rows.lit: But he'll surely come home, right? Together with my father.
rows.re: But he'll surely come home, / right? Together with my father.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @But I know I'll recognize him when he finally comes home!
rows.jp: 「でもね、帰って来たら / すぐにわかるはずだよ
rows.lit: But when he comes home, I'll know him right away.
rows.re: But when he comes home, I'll know / him right away.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @After all, he's my father!
rows.jp: 「だって、俺のお<b:8a79>さんだもの<b:8a79>さんが帰ってくるんだよ
rows.lit: After all, he's my father.
rows.re: After all, he's my father.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @Mother and I are waiting for him, just like we did yesterday and the day before and the day before that.
rows.jp: 「だから、<b:8a7d>回もおとといも / その前の回も / ずーっと、お<b:8a7a>さんと待っているんだ<b:8a7e>える[11]ぉと / ヘキサロックと呼ばれる / <b:8a7f><894b>面の<b:8a80>谷がある
rows.lit: So yesterday, the day before, and the day before that, I've waited with Mother all this while.
rows.re: So yesterday, the day before, and / before that, I've waited with / Mother all this while.
rows.speaker: widow's son

rows.en: @According to the ancient texts, the castle of the Crimson Nobles is at the base of that mountain.
rows.jp: 「<b:8a81><b:8a82>によると / そのふもとにこそ / 『ノーブルレッド』の館があるという
rows.lit: According to the old texts, it's at that mountain's foot that the castle of the "Crimson Nobles" stands.
rows.re: By the old texts, it's at that / mountain's foot that the |Crimson / Nobles|' castle stands.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @But scaling the steep face of Mt. Urartu would seem to be a daunting task indeed.
rows.jp: 「だが、この<b:8a83>険なるウラルトゥの谷<b:8a84>を / <b:8a7e>えることが / どれほどまでに<b:8a85><b:8a86>なことであろうか〜<b:8a87>斬して / 自らの<b:8a88>とするという〜
rows.lit: But scaling the perilous face of Mt. Urartu; what a formidable task that would be.
rows.re: But scaling the perilous face of / Mt. Urartu; what a formidable / task that would be.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Even more amazing, they can absorb the special abilities of many kinds of monsters.
rows.jp: 「また、<8845><b:8a89>すべきは / 年多のモンスター<b:8a5f>が得意とする / 結単能力をも取り込むことができるらしい
rows.lit: What's more striking, they can even absorb the special abilities many monsters excel at.
rows.re: What's more striking, they can / even absorb the special abilities / many monsters excel at.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Today the Crimson Nobles live only in legend. I wonder why they disappeared.
rows.jp: 「だが、なぜに / 『ノーブルレッド』は<b:8a78>を消し / 伝説の中に生きるのみなのだろうか？
rows.lit: But why did the "Crimson Nobles" vanish, living on only in legend?
rows.re: But why did the |Crimson Nobles| / vanish, living on only in legend?
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Sunlight doesn't harm us, but to the Crimson Nobles it was like beingsliced by burning-hot swords.
rows.jp: 「それは<b:8a8a>輝〜 / 我々には、何てこと無い<b:8a8b><b:8a8a>の輝であるが / 彼らにとっては<b:8a8c><8868>の<b:8a8d>に<b:8a8e>しいという
rows.lit: It was the sunlight; nothing to us, but to them it was like being cut by burning blades.
rows.re: It was the sunlight; nothing to / us, but to them like being cut by / burning blades.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @Now that the sun has been devoured, I imagine conditions on Filgaia would be perfect for them.
rows.jp: 「空を失い、<b:8a8b><b:8a8a>無き今〜 / 伝説に生きる彼らが<b:8a8f>び目信めるには / もっとも相応しい状況ではなかろうか<b:8a90>の<b:8a91>女＞の時代には / 人の<b:8a92>命を<8995>かに<b:8a7e>える / イモータル（幻<b:8a7e>者）がいたという
rows.lit: With the sky lost and no sunlight now, could conditions be more fitting for those legend-dwellers to wake?
rows.re: With the sky lost and no sunlight / now, could conditions better suit / those legend-dwellers to wake?
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @The legend of the Crimson Nobles -- a proud, red-blooded race -- still lives here in Mt. Urartu.
rows.jp: 「『ノーブルレッド』〜 / 高<b:8a93>なる眠き<b:8a94>の一<b:8a95>とされた者の伝説が / このウラルトゥの谷に残されているのだ<b:8a62>ん中[11]ぉに / <8a13><b:8a3b><b:8a42><b:8a43>ギルドグラードがあるんだ
rows.lit: The "Crimson Nobles"; the legend of that proud, red-blooded race lingers here in Mt. Urartu.
rows.re: The |Crimson Nobles|; the legend / of that proud, red-blooded race / lingers here in Mt. Urartu.
rows.speaker: scholar

rows.en: @They built their thriving industry by mining fossils of ancient organo-mechanical creatures.
rows.jp: 「機艇とも生物ともつかない / 古代生物の『合谷』によって / 発<b:8a96>を<89d8>げたってのは作名な話だ
rows.lit: It's a famous tale: they built their boom on the "fossils" of ancient creatures, half-machine, half-beast.
rows.re: It's a famous tale: they built / their boom on the fossils of / half-machine ancient creatures.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @I think a lot of other ancient secrets and relics still lie undiscovered in this area.
rows.jp: 「僕はこの地には / 古代からの発<b:8a97>や遺<b:8a3a>が / まだまだ<89bb>っているとにらんでいるんだが〜<b:8a52> / 「ああ〜 <b:8a98>物陸<b:8a99>が〜〜
rows.lit: I reckon this land still holds plenty of ancient secrets and relics yet undiscovered.
rows.re: I reckon this land still holds / plenty of ancient secrets and / relics yet undiscovered.
rows.speaker: townsperson

rows.en: @Anyway, please take good care of young master Noel.
rows.jp: 「と、とりあえず / ノエルぼっちゃんをお願いします〜<f05b>
rows.lit: A-anyway, please look after young master Noel.
rows.re: A-anyway, please look after young / master Noel.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.en: @relieved that you seem quite normal. Being guarded by stern types can get quite tiring.
rows.jp: 「<b:8a9a>通の方でよかった / あんまりスゴイ人たちに護衛されても / <b:8a9b><b:8a4f>ですからね<b:8a52> / 「本回は、ノエルぼっちゃまの / 護衛をよろしくお願いします
rows.lit: I'm glad they're ordinary folk; being guarded by anyone too grand would only be uncomfortable.
rows.re: I'm glad they're ordinary folk; / being guarded by anyone too grand / would be uncomfortable.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @You'll be heading straight to Guild Galad, with no stops. After all, we can't be too careful.
rows.jp: 「この<b:8a9c>からいっきに / ギルドグラードへ向かいますが / なにぶん、用心にこした事はありません
rows.lit: From here you head straight for Guild Galad; but you can never be too careful.
rows.re: From here you head straight for / Guild Galad; but you can never be / too careful.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.en: @Please, don't let those villains of Odessa harm master Noel.
rows.jp: 「<b:8a9d>を<b:8a5c>がす悪<b:8a9e>オデッサより / どうかお護りください<b:8a52> / 「では、そろそろ / 発陸時<89c2>がまいります
rows.lit: Please guard him from those villains of Odessa who threaten the peace.
rows.re: Please guard him from those / villains of Odessa who threaten / the peace.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.en: @Please start boarding now.
rows.jp: 「陸<b:8a99>の方までお願いします
rows.lit: Please begin boarding now.
rows.re: Please begin boarding now.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.en: @I was expecting something ornate and glittery.
rows.jp: 「もっとド派手で / 金ピカの乗り物を想<b:8a9f>していたんだ〜<b:8a3b><b:8a42><b:8a43>ギルドグラードの<b:8aa0>品は / <b:8aa1><b:8aa2>を<b:8aa3>まず、質を追<b:8aa4>します
rows.lit: I'd pictured something far flashier, all gold and glitter.
rows.re: I'd pictured something far / flashier, all gold and glitter.
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @We emphasize functionality above all else.
rows.jp: 「何よりも / その機能性を重要視するのです
rows.lit: Above all else, we prize functionality.
rows.re: Above all else, we prize / functionality.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @What need does the son of Guild Galad Master have for a pompously decorated train?
rows.jp: 「わたくしが乗るからといって / <b:8aa5><b:8aa6>に<b:8aa7>られた<89dc>陸など / 用意することはありませんよ
rows.lit: Just because I'm aboard is no reason to lay on a gaudily decorated train.
rows.re: Just because I'm aboard is no / reason to lay on a gaudily / decorated train.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @And, besides, I love the Dianbai Guang. I'd rather ride this train than any other.
rows.jp: 「〜それに、わたくしは / この『<89de><89df>輝』が大<b:8aa3>きですから / むしろ、うれしいくらいです<b:8a52> / 「ぼっちゃん、お話しは陸街でお願いします
rows.lit: Besides, I love this "Dianbai Guang"; if anything, it makes me glad.
rows.re: Besides, I love this |Dianbai / Guang|; if anything, it makes me / glad.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @Your father will reprimand me if the train doesn't depart on time!
rows.jp: 「定<89c2>通りに<b:8aa8>着しないと / お<b:8a79>上に私が<b:8aa9>られてしまいますッ！
rows.lit: If we don't arrive on schedule, your father will have my hide!
rows.re: If we don't arrive on schedule, / your father will have my hide!
rows.speaker: conductor

rows.en: @But we had to sacrifice it to save you.
rows.jp: 「キミを護るためとはいえ / <b:8a98>物陸<b:8a99>を<b:8aaa><b:8aab>にしてしまった
rows.lit: To protect you, we've had to sacrifice the cargo cars.
rows.re: To protect you, we've had to / sacrifice the cargo cars.
rows.speaker: conductor

rows.en: @My father hired you to guard me, and you have done that job splendidly.
rows.jp: 「みなさんが<b:8a79>から<8923>頼されたのは / あくまでも、わたくしの護衛〜 / 任務は立派に果たしているではありませんか<b:8a52> / 「では、ぼっちゃん / わたしたちは<f040><f042><b:8aac>理をお願いします
rows.lit: What Father charged you with was, above all, my protection; and you've performed it splendidly.
rows.re: What Father charged you with was, / above all, my protection; and / you've done it splendidly.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @We'll go on ahead and return to Guild Galad at once.
rows.jp: 「わたくしたちは / 単行動でギルドグラードまで / 先に戻らせてもらいます
rows.lit: We'll go on ahead separately and return to Guild Galad first.
rows.re: We'll go on ahead separately and / return to Guild Galad first.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.en: @If I don't get back soon, Father will be furious.
rows.jp: 「急いで『わたくし』を続けないと / <b:8a79>上がまた<b:8aad>りだすかもしれませんから
rows.lit: I'd best hurry back to my duties, or Father may start fuming again.
rows.re: I'd best hurry back to my duties, / or Father may start fuming again.
rows.speaker: Noel

rows.en: @Guild Galad is located on reclaimed land 1northeast0 of this station.
rows.jp: 「ギルドグラードは / このステーションを出て / [11]お北側[11]ぉの<89db>め立て地にあります
rows.lit: Guild Galad lies on the reclaimed land to the [11]north side[11], out from this station.
rows.re: Guild Galad lies on the reclaimed / land to the [11]north side[11], / out from this station.
rows.speaker: attendant

rows.jp: ＊進みますか？[18]か
rows.lit: Do you want to proceed?
rows.re: Do you want to proceed?
rows.speaker: system/prompt

rows.en: @Unfortunately, this service is unavailable in the Demo Version.
rows.jp: 「<f040><f042>でも、今回の体験版では / 残念ながら使用することができません
rows.lit: But in this trial version, it unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.re: But in this trial version, it / unfortunately cannot be used.
rows.speaker: system/prompt

rows.jp: ＊〜ですが、今回の体験版では / 残念ながら使用することができません

rows.jp: ＊ＨＰの回右<886f>は / ゲットしたジェムの大きさに比<8943>し / その乗果はパーティー全置におよびます着のふちに向かって / 方向キーを入れたままにすると / 『おっとっと』ポーズをとることがあります

rows.re: *You can also jump down by dashing / off an edge, no |oops| needed.
rows.speaker: tutorial

rows.en: @I refuse to abandon my mission!
rows.jp: 「任務を放棄することはできないッ！<b:8a65> / [ff][ff][0a]<b:8a65> / [ff][ff][0b]<b:8a65> / [ff][ff][0c]
rows.lit: We can't abandon the mission!
rows.re: We can't abandon the mission!
rows.speaker: Musketeer, pushing in

rows.en: @The monsters are multiplying here because these treacherous ruins have been left abandoned.
rows.jp: 「こんな危険な遺跡を / 野放しにしているから / モンスターが増えていくんだよ同胞隊置 / 「何だって僕たち同胞隊が / こんなトコまで出<b:8a3e>らなきゃいけないんだ
rows.lit: It's because dangerous ruins like this are left unchecked that the monsters keep multiplying.
rows.re: It's because dangerous ruins like / this are left unchecked that the / monsters keep multiplying.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @Hey, 0. Shouldn't we leave the search of the ruins to the |Mercs?|
rows.jp: 「なあ、[05]ぉ / 遺跡漁りなんてのは『渡り烏』の連中に / まかせた方がいいと思わねェか？<b:8a41>きはしないぜ守れないヤツは一人前ではない
rows.lit: Hey, {5}, don't you think ruin-scavenging is better left to the "Mercs"?
rows.re: Hey, {5}, don't you think / ruin-scavenging is better left to / the "Mercs"?

rows.jp: 「誘拐犯人グループは３人 / どうやらタウンメリアの場まで / 出稼ぎに来ていた季節労働者らしい同胞隊置 / 「犯人はもともと / スレイハイム国の出身らしい
rows.lit: The kidnapper group is three; laborers, it seems, who came as far as Town Meria for seasonal work.
rows.re: The kidnapper group is three; / laborers, it seems, who came as far / as Town Meria for seasonal work.
rows.speaker: Musketeer, on the culprits

rows.en: @Slayheim is the western country that was defeated in a war 5 years ago.
rows.jp: 「〜<88d2>数前の街戦で、消失してしまった / あのスレイハイム国だ同胞隊置 / 「お前も気がついていると思うが / 最近、モンスターが増えてきているだろう？
rows.lit: The culprits are originally from Slayheim, they say; that Slayheim that vanished in the war a few years back.
rows.re: The culprits hail from Slayheim, / they say. That kingdom that / vanished in the war years ago.
rows.speaker: Musketeer, on Slayheim

rows.en: @With the world so unstable, it'll only get worse.
rows.jp: 「世情が不安定になると / こういった事件も増えていくんだ
rows.lit: When the state of the world grows unstable, incidents like this multiply too.
rows.re: When the state of the world grows / unstable, incidents like this / multiply too.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @There are going to be more and more people like this.
rows.jp: 「まだまだ増えるぜ / こういった輩がよ〜同胞隊置 / 「もしもバトルで倒れるようなことがあっても / 『コンティニュー』すればだいじょうぶだ
rows.re: There'll be more and more of these / types around.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @You'll return to the condition you were in before the battle and get to redo it.
rows.jp: 「そのバトルに / 突入した時の状態まで戻るから / やりなおしができるのだ
rows.re: You snap back to how you were / before the fight and redo it.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @The |Continue| system is convenient but its use is limited.
rows.jp: 「便利なシステム『コンティニュー』ッ！ / だけど、その使用回年には限りがある

rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @Each time you hit |Continue| one Gimel Coin is spent.
rows.jp: 「１回、コンティニューを行うたびに / アイテム『１ギミルコイン』を / ひとつ消費してしまうのだ
rows.re: Each |Continue| costs you one Gimel / Coin.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.en: @Gimel Coins are very valuable, so use them wisely. They should only be used as a last resort!!
rows.jp: 「１ギミルコインは貴重なアイテムだからな / その使いどきを誤るなよ / コンティニューは、最後の手段なのだッ！同胞隊置 / 「この遺跡には / めぼしいお宝なんて残っていやしないぜ
rows.lit: There's no treasure worth mentioning left in these ruins.
rows.re: There's no treasure worth / mentioning left in these ruins.
rows.speaker: Musketeer, on the ruins

rows.lit: Long ago it was picked nearly clean by the adventurers called "Mercs".
rows.re: Long ago it was picked nearly clean / by the adventurers called "Mercs".
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.jp: 「ここが『枯れた遺跡』と呼ばれるのは / そういうことからさ同胞隊置 / 「どうやらこのあたりは / すでにモンスターのテリトリーらしい
rows.lit: That's why this place is called "the Withered Ruins".
rows.re: That's why this place is called / "the Withered Ruins".
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.jp: 「気を招き締めていくぞッ！同胞隊置 / 「すでに調査<8994>みの遺跡だからって / 気は抜けないぞ

rows.jp: 「この先、どんな仕<89eb>けがあるのか / 見当もつかないからな同胞隊置 / 「すまない〜 / 世話をかけるな同胞隊置 / 「あのオッチョコチョイめ〜
[17]<b:8a56>ったヤツが / そこの<b:8a57>に転落してしまったのだ

rows.lit: Sorry, but could you go and take a look around?
rows.re: Sorry, but could you go and take a / look around?
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.jp: 「ここで目立った手柄でもたてて / ウワサの新設部隊への / 転属なんかねらっちまうからこのザマだ来るまでここにいた方がいい同胞隊置 / 「そうもしてらんねぇよ / ホラ、ちょっと見ておきなッ！同胞隊置 / 「〜〜ッ！[17]

rows.re: This is what you get for chasing a / flashy feat to angle for a transfer / to that rumored new unit.

rows.jp: 「さっきのようにスイッチを入れる以外にも / 使い道があるかもしれんな〜 / そいつは自分で探すことだ同胞隊置 / 「ここの上の足場に気をつけろ / 崩れる前<b:8a5c>に<88f7>意を<b:8a5d>うのだッ！

rows.re: Slip up and fall, and you'll get / stuck like me.
rows.speaker: Musketeer

rows.jp: 「あの２人 / どこからか徴同されてきたばかりか？

rows.jp: 「そこからもう少し辺に / 小さなスイッチブロックがあるでしょ？姉 / 「さっきと同じ要領で / あなたの魔力を反応させてみて〜

rows.speaker: Sister

rows.lit: Come back here and I'll cast Recovery Magic, so don't push yourself too hard.

rows.re: Do your best, {2}. Two Switchblocks / left.
rows.speaker: Sister

rows.en: @This was nothing.
rows.jp: 「このくらい / どうってことないよ姉 / 「お姉ちゃんは、お姉ちゃん / あなたは、あなたなのよ
rows.lit: This much is nothing. Believe in yourself more strongly.
rows.re: This much is nothing. Believe in / yourself more strongly.
rows.speaker: Sister

rows.en: @You need to believe in yourself more.
rows.jp: 「もっと、自分を強く信じて〜
rows.lit: Believe in yourself more strongly.
rows.re: Believe in yourself more strongly.
rows.speaker: Sister

rows.en: @2, from now on you need to believe in the magic that is yours alone.
rows.jp: 「[05]か〜 / これから先、あなたしか使えない / 『魔法』を強く信じて
rows.lit: {2}... from here on, believe deeply in the magic that only you can use.
rows.re: {2}... from here on, believe deeply / in the magic that only you can use.
rows.speaker: Sister

rows.en: @No matter how hard things get, you'll be able to overcome it with your magic.
rows.jp: 「どんなにつらいことがあっても / あなたの『魔法』なら / 乗り越えられていけるから〜ね
rows.lit: No matter how painful things get, your magic will carry you through.
rows.re: No matter how painful things get, / your magic will carry you through.
rows.speaker: Sister

rows.en: @Later! Leave it 'til later!
rows.jp: 「そんなのあと、あとッ！

rows.re: That stuff's for later, later!
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.jp: 「わたしの『魔法』で / ぜーんぶ何とかしたら / いくらでも聞くからさッ！
rows.lit: Once I've handled everything with MY magic, I'll listen to as much as you want!
rows.re: Once I've handled everything with / MY magic, I'll listen to as much as / you want!
rows.speaker: Lilka

rows.en: @Soon, you'll be linked to the world you came from, so don't worry.
rows.jp: 「もうすぐ / もといた世界にリンクされるから〜 / あなたは何も心配しなくていいから〜〜姉ちゃんはッ！姉 / [14][15]ぉか「ね、〜いごに〜とつだけ / や〜そくして〜〜[16]くぉ[16]くぉ[0c][15]ぉき「〜う、〜〜〜いで / 〜〜て〜 [05]か〜[16]くぉ[16]くぉ[17]姉ちゃんッ！
rows.lit: Soon you'll be linked back to the world you came from, so you needn't worry about a thing.
rows.re: Soon you'll be linked back to the / world you came from, so you needn't / worry about a thing.

rows.en: @Even I thought for a second that it might come out.
rows.jp: 「もしかしたら抜けるんじゃないかって / 俺も一<b:8a39>、思ってしまったくらいさ<b:8a3a>、誰もあの<b:8a3b>を<f040><f042> / 『アガートラーム』を / 抜くことなんてできなかったな〜
rows.lit: For a moment even I thought maybe it could be drawn.
rows.re: For a moment even I thought maybe / it could be drawn.
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.jp: 「あの<b:8a3b>が抜けるようなことがあるってことは / それなりの理由があるってことだろ？<b:8a3b>を抜けるモノ<f040><f042> / それって『勇者』なんだろ？
rows.lit: If that sword can be drawn at all, it must mean there's some reason for it, right?
rows.re: If that sword can be drawn at / all, it must mean there's some / reason for it, right?
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.en: @A |hero| suddenly appearing means there will be some disturbance needing a |hero.|
rows.jp: 「『勇者』が<890c>生するってことは / 『勇者』を必要とする / 何らかの戦<8945>があるってことじゃないか

rows.re: But well... maybe that's just how / it is.
rows.speaker: soldier

rows.re: After all, nobody wants war.
